Title: Incomplete multi-character sanitization in DOCX text extraction (entity-decode-after-tag-strip ordering)
Description: Tag-stripping (removing <...> sequences) runs BEFORE XML-entity decoding. An entity-encoded fake tag in a DOCX's document.xml (e.g. text content containing the literal characters <script>) is not touched by the tag-stripper (it contains no raw < or > characters at that point) and is then decoded afterward into a literal <script> string in the extracted CV text.
Fix Commit: Verified NOT currently exploitable: extracted CV text (baseCvText and similar) is only ever consumed via plain React JSX interpolation, AI-prompt input, or heuristic string matching downstream (confirmed via grep of all consumers) - no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML assignment, or Markdown-to-HTML rendering path exists anywhere in apps/web (independently confirmed by the SEC-002 review). If a future code path ever renders this text as raw HTML, this becomes a real stored-XSS vector via a malicious uploaded CV.
Retest Result: Decode XML entities BEFORE stripping tags
Residual Risk: or repeat tag-stripping after decode until no more matches (the standard fix pattern CodeQL's own advisory recommends). Small
column15: Not yet fixed - recommended for Phase 3 follow-up
column17: Low given no current rendering sink; would become High if reintroduced downstream without fixing this first

Title: ZAP passive scan: User Controllable HTML Element Attribute (Potential XSS) on /compatibility
Evidence: ZAP flagged one instance where a query-string parameter value appears to influence an HTML element attribute on the /compatibility page (used for pre-filling an anonymous extension bug-report form). This is a passive heuristic finding - ZAP did not confirm actual script execution.
Impact: ZAP baseline run 2026-08-21 log output (WARN-NEW x1)
Remediation: Unconfirmed. This assessment did not independently verify exploitability (e.g. attempting an actual attribute-breakout payload) given the operating rule against active scanning/attacks on the real production site without separate authorisation. Needs a manual, deliberate verification pass in Phase 3 using a safe crafted payload against a local/test instance, not production.
Fix Commit: Verify with a targeted local test: submit a crafted company/description value and inspect the rendered attribute for breakout. Fix (if confirmed) is standard attribute-context escaping.
Status: Unknown pending verification - treat as open until confirmed safe or fixed

Title: ZAP passive scan: CSP script-src unsafe-inline / missing Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy
Evidence: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' for script-src; no COEP header is set.
Impact: ZAP baseline run 2026-08-21 log output (WARN-NEW x10 / x5)
Remediation: Not a new finding - this is a previously documented, deliberate deferral (docs/quality-assurance.md #99): removing unsafe-inline needs a nonce-based CSP threaded through every inline script/style including third-party embeds (Stripe, PostHog); COEP would require every cross-origin resource to opt in via its own CORP/CORS headers, real risk of breaking checkout/analytics for no practical benefit given no SharedArrayBuffer/cross-origin-isolation need exists today.
Fix Commit: No new remediation recommended this pass - re-confirmed as an accepted
Retest Result: documented risk. Revisit only if a genuine cross-origin-isolation requirement emerges.
Residual Risk: N/A - accepted risk from a prior assessment
column16: Closed - re-confirmed as an existing accepted risk

Title: No structural backstop preventing a future API route from omitting its auth check
Description: apps/web has no middleware.ts - every route independently calls the correct auth helper as a matter of convention, not enforcement. A full manual sweep of all 53 route files this pass found ZERO current gaps (46 AUTH-OK, 7 documented intentionally-public), but the discipline has no lint rule or shared wrapper backstopping it for future routes.
Remediation: None today - this is a forward-looking hardening recommendation, not a current vulnerability. A future PR adding a new route could plausibly omit the auth check with nothing catching it before code review.
Fix Commit: Consider a lint rule or a required withAuth/withAdminAuth wrapper convention so a missing check fails at build/review time rather than relying on every future author remembering the pattern.
